title: Empirica host-boundary registry
authority: This file is the authoritative host-boundary registry (ADR-0068, ADR-0069): ids, boundary, outcomes per host and per control mode, sources, and the scenario rows with the tests (`covered_by`) or ledger rows (`live_only`, `ledger_rows`) that settle them. doc/design/empirica-host-boundary-registry.md owns the prose; its data parts are generated from this file (`make registry-doc`), and `make contract-check` fails on any drift, on a reference that does not resolve, on a covering test that does not exist, and on a ledger row that does not exist.

bounds.definition: With K = 3 and T = 16: the K-th turn end of a chain on one observation basis, or the T-th turn end in a chain, ends the chain with the `unattended_residual` notice, so at most K − 1 continuations on one basis and T − 1 in a chain. The last continuation before a bound, the (K − 1)-th on one basis or the (T − 1)-th in a chain, carries `unattended_residual` as its directive, so the model is offered the stop while it is still reading. A changed basis restarts the count on the new basis; any turn end that is not a continuation ends the chain and clears both counts. A continuation that carries the `unattended_residual` directive (the actor `none`) counts like any other.

outcomes.allow: End the turn: the run converged and the view says so (`Allow(converged=true)` is the only convergence claim).
outcomes.settle: End the turn with the run view and no notice: exactly one audit is pending and its result continues the run.
outcomes.settle-notice: End the turn with the contract notice of the settlement; the run stays active and not converged, and nothing was approved or confirmed by the settlement.
outcomes.pause: End the turn with a contract notice that is not a convergence claim and names the real next step the human can relay to the agent; the run stays active, nobody was asked, nothing was granted. The same on a first and a later turn end.
outcomes.continue: Keep the turn going: the agent is handed the next obligation (the core's real reason on the first turn end of a chain; `unattended_continue`, which asks it to act on the reason, on a later one; `unattended_residual` as the directive on the last continuation before a bound, the one text of the chain the model is sure to read). Progress is one fact with one owner: the core's `run.basis` (`core.evaluation.progress_basis`), which both hosts remember at their last continuation and compare, and nothing else. A chain is bounded by `bounds`: the K-th turn end on one basis and the T-th in a chain end it instead (`end-no-progress`).
outcomes.end-no-progress: End the chain because it reached its bound (`bounds`), or because the `none` actor's one continuation on a basis was spent: the notice is `unattended_residual`, the one notice that offers `report_convergence intent=stop` as the honest end. Pi records `no-progress`.
outcomes.unreachable: The state cannot arise in this control mode (the core never produces it there); no host outcome is defined, and a scenario names the test that proves it.
outcomes.continue-with-notice: Keep the turn going with the cell's notice as the directive, once per observation basis: the run needs a decision from the agent (end honestly, or revise the claim graph), and a settled turn would hand it to nobody. The continuation is counted like any other (`bounds`), and a turn end on the basis the previous one saw ends the chain instead with `unattended_residual` (`end-no-progress`).

states.title: exactly one async audit is pending

the sole blocker is a configuration a human is asked to approve (`turn_end_actor` `human`): the first approval, or in interactive auto after its first approval a budget raise; a delegated auto run has no human to ask

the sole blocker is an exhausted budget and the core offers no `budget.raise`: a deliberative run's, and a delegated auto run's (before investigation nothing is exhausted, and interactive auto after its first approval is always offered the raise)

the sole blocker is an exhausted budget and the core offers `budget.raise`: a deliberative human decides it, and interactive auto after its first approval offers it to the agent to propose for its human to approve, so the turn goes on (a delegated auto run is never offered it, and before investigation nothing is exhausted)

the sole blocker is an evidence confirmation, which only a deliberative run's human can be asked about; an auto run asks no one, so the state does not arise there (a source that needs a human is inert, and the author gets the claim's own reason, `active-other`)

the run's `turn_end_actor` is `none`: the root claim is refuted or conflicted, so the claims cannot be approved as they stand; a deliberative human decides, and an auto run's agent is handed the choice to end honestly or revise the claim graph
any other active, non-converged state: the author has a step to take (`turn_end_actor` `author`), or the view does not say

claude.settle: exit 0; the run view (async audit) or `systemMessage` with the notice
claude.continue: exit 2 with the reason on stderr (the real reason), and `unattended_continue` when `stop_hook_active` is true; the last continuation before a bound carries `unattended_residual` on stderr; the K-th turn end on one `run.basis`, or the T-th in the chain, ends the chain (exit 0, `systemMessage`) with `unattended_residual`
claude.loop_bound: Claude's `stop_hook_active` plus its own cap of eight consecutive continuations, which resets each time Claude calls a tool, so it bounds a run of continuations without a tool call and no productive chain (`host-capped` when it is reached). A deliberative pause ends the turn (ADR-0068 owns the `stop_hook_active` rule). The adapter applies `bounds` as Pi does: it remembers `{run, basis, count, total}` per session, in a file written atomically, and reads it only on a Stop that follows a blocked one (`stop_hook_active` true) and only for the run it was written for; a changed basis restarts `count` at 1, every continuation adds one to `total`, any outcome that is not a continuation clears the record, and a record it cannot read (a bare basis from an older version, or a malformed one) reads as a changed basis with zeroed counts. A `systemMessage` of an exit-0 Stop is shown to the user, so the model is offered the stop in the stderr of the last continuation.

pi.event: `agent_before_settle` only (never `turn_end`, so one notice per settle); Pi 1.0.0 and later
pi.settle: nothing is appended, or a `custom_message` (`display: true`) with the settlement notice
pi.pause: append a `custom_message` entry (`display: true`) holding the notice, with no `continue`
pi.continue: `continue: true`, with the next obligation as the appended message; the last continuation before a bound appends `unattended_residual`
pi.loop_bound: None from the host. The adapter keeps its own, in memory only: it remembers `{basis, count, total}` for the chain it is in and applies `bounds`: a changed basis restarts `count` at 1, every continuation adds one to `total`, and the K-th turn end on a basis or the T-th in the chain ends with the `unattended_residual` notice and records `no-progress`. Any outcome that is not a continuation clears the memory, and so do the end of the run, a change of run and a new prompt; a memory it cannot read (a bare basis from an older version, or a malformed one) reads as a changed basis with zeroed counts.

expectations.title: compaction never changes what the run knows
expectations.outcomes:
- Claude: `SessionStart` matcher `compact` → `RestoreRun` → bounded run view on stdout, then one line saying the claim graph is not in the view and is read with `empirica_read` `GetArgument`, exit 0 always; orphaned pending audits are reconciled first (`reconcile_orphans(…, include_pending=False)`). A restore failure writes one diagnostic line and exits 0. `PreCompact` is not used (it could block compaction, which Empirica does not).
- Pi: `session_before_compact` is not handled, so Pi keeps its own summary. `session_compact` dispatches `RestoreRun` and sends one `empirica` message (`triggerTurn: false`: it never starts or continues a turn), carrying the handle, the rendered run view as untrusted data, and the line saying the claim graph is not in the view and is read with `empirica_read` `GetArgument`. It is delivered in the next model request without starting a turn (a `context` handler adds it until its entry is in the history, and at most until the first `agent_end`) and persisted as one `empirica` message. A restore failure sends the handle line only; a terminal run or no handle sends nothing; nothing throws. `session_compact_failed` is not handled.
- Codex: `SessionStart` source `compact` re-evaluates.
expectations.sources: QREF `restore_after_compaction`, ADR-33, T1 §1 ("Restore/compaction must preserve …"), `V2/test_evidence_scenarios.py::RestoreCells::test_everything_the_human_gate_depends_on_survives_a_reload_and_a_restore`, `CT/test_activation_lifecycle.py::test_restore_is_silent_and_exit_zero`, `PT/gate.test.ts` ("after compaction one Empirica message carries the handle, the rendered run view and the GetArgument recovery line", "compaction never forces a turn: the message is sent with triggerTurn:false, never steered, in every reason", "the next request carries the restore text exactly once; once the durable entry exists the context handler adds nothing", "the bridge is bounded: with no durable entry it is added to requests until the first agent_end, then to none", "after compaction a RestoreRun failure sends the handle line only and never throws", "after compaction a terminal run, or no handle, sends nothing", "a different run taking over during the restore sends nothing", "the whole restore message for the largest measured state stays under the ceiling", "with no restore pending the context handler is a no-op").

expectations.title: the qualify action is one long host-effect operation, and its refusal passes through unchanged
expectations.outcomes: All hosts while the qualify effect has not landed: the core decides `qualify`'s admission and refuses — `environment-required`, `environment-pending`, `environment-rejected`, `environment-revisions-exhausted` or `qualification-attempts-exhausted` where the admission fails, and exactly the `environment.not_available` Block where it passes — returning through the composed core surface unchanged: no attempt charged, no binding change; the `environment` proposal action is admitted after configuration approval and investigation admission with the exclusion mutual both ways (refused while a configuration is pending; a configuration revision admitted while an environment revision is pending closes that revision superseded without approval), so the E6 family's refusal-of-everything is ended, and the per-run revision ceiling keeps every revision and its receipts immutable and refuses a further submission with its own closed reason past the contract bound. What the current deterministic tests cover stops at the composed service: the transport and effect half — the Block passing through the host surface with no transport wait or retry, and no host launching Docker or falling back to a host shell — is a host-side fact with no evidence yet, pending the effect and the transports (E9/E12/E13), not a demonstrated claim. A terminal run's observation stays `inert`. Pi once the cycle lands: the exact `qualify` ObserveAction joins the long-operation class beside `spike_request` (`isExactSpikeRequest`'s classifier), so its outer transport margin is the long one, while the core's own attempt deadline (lock wait, recovery, up to 16 inspections, the five probes, cleanup, publication) bounds the host effect; a killed or timed-out attempt binds nothing. Claude once the cycle lands: the MCP call keeps its outer margin and adds no elicitation of its own; the attempt journalling and recovery are the bridge's. Codex: no support is claimed while its host port is composed out; nothing here promises any Codex long-operation classification.

scenarios.setup: an approved configuration with route and investigation recorded, so a closed `environment` action admits a pending revision on the fetched document's run
scenarios.action: the Claude session mediates `empirica_observe` with a closed `environment` action: it fetches the pending revision's private document pair, publishes it write-first through the one sidecar helper, presents one receipt, elicits the approval form, and decides
scenarios.expected: the sidecar file already holds exactly the document's bytes (mode 0400) before the present receipt reaches the service, and the present and the decision name the same fetched digest — the receipt's own revision and proposal digest come from the bound document, never from adapter state. The fetched document is refused before any write unless it names this run, the environment kind and the proposal digest of the very revision the action admitted (a revision-one fetch injected into revision two, another run's document and a valid document of another kind each leave the receipt journal and the sidecar directory untouched). The native form stays short and keeps what the human decides by: the goal, the container profile with the networked one called out inside the first three lines Claude Code shows (`NETWORK EGRESS ENABLED`, from the schema's two-way `networked` pair), the spike image count and the document's exact `File:` path — never a decision link, because the observer projects no environment decision yet (E11); the agent's plan under "the agent's plan — not verified", the author's unverified rationale, the image references and the installed binding live in the bound document, each under its own label. An accept approves the revision, a decline rejects it, a cancel, a timeout or an answer under a foreign request id leaves it pending with only the presentation row and no decision; an impostor or stale document digest refuses with `environment.document_mismatch` before any row is written, and the host's one same-revision re-present (fetch again, present again, then stop) is the executable recovery. A host surface without a form asks nobody: the admitted action is returned with the revision pending. The environment mediation and its private fetch and decision are composed for the Claude Code host alone: a Codex-profile session composes none, and a profile whose approval ingress is not the one the run's human episode recorded (or has none) reads no document and records no receipt, even sharing the run's repository. The document text itself validates as `empirica.hitl/1` against the schema's additive third kind, escapes every free-text value through the core's one escaper and bounds each escaped string by the proposal's own bound times the escaper's longest expansion. Pi's dialog is E12's and is not claimed here.

scenarios.setup: an active run in each admission state (no revision, one pending, one approved), in any bootstrap state
scenarios.action: the model calls `empirica_observe` with a closed `qualify` action (and, in the same family, `environment`)
scenarios.expected: one Block carrying `qualify`'s own closed admission reason when the admission fails, and exactly the missing-effect reason `environment.not_available` once a revision is approved while the effect has not landed — no attempt charged, no binding changed, an unchanged run view in both cases; on a terminal run the observation is inert instead. The family's mutual exclusion and ceiling hold the same way: a configuration revision admitted while an environment revision is pending closes it superseded without approval (its rows immutable), and a submission past the per-run revision ceiling refuses with `environment-revisions-exhausted` while nothing is ever evicted; the same family bounds each revision's private presentations (128, a per-revision allowance separate from the revision ceiling): a further presentation past it refuses with `environment-presentations-exhausted`, while one the revision already recorded can still finalize and a new revision starts a fresh allowance. Covered by in-process dispatch tests only: surface pass-through on a host transport, no transport wait or retry, and the absence of any host effect (no container, no host-shell fallback) are deliberately not claimed yet — those scenarios stay pending until the effect and the transports land (E9/E12/E13). Since E8 the same family completes its write-first path: a presentation may name only the digest of the document the core renders for the pending revision — the pair the private fetch returns and the host writes before it presents — so a present under any other digest refuses with `environment.document_mismatch` (nothing written, no allowance spent) exactly as a stale document from an earlier revision does, while every decision keeps being bound first by its own recorded presentation (an impostor decision digest stays the engine's fail-closed replay refusal, and approve and reject both close only under the fetched document's digest).
